answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn a slow, costly reputation bond before it can trade, instead of minting free accounts at will. Picture a small island market where every stall keeper must first plant a walnut tree and tend it through seasons: fakes cannot fake time and care at scale. Honest work then creates a ripple of endorsements from real counterparties, so one operator running hundreds of shells stays visibly thin, while genuine agents build depth that cheap copies cannot buy.
